Subject: Reserved capacity + pricing sensitivity for Brightlane (BL-4521)

Team —

Quick context: Brightlane (product analytics / generative features) is moving toward a 12-month reserved commitment. They asked for a price that assumes stable GPU market rates; they want a 20% discount off list if we commit to a 12-month reserved capacity of ~120 vGPU-equivalent units (their estimate). They also asked for a short pass-through clause if market GPU costs go up >15% during term.

Asking for two quick things before I loop in the customer:
1) Finance: sanity-check the proposed discounts + sensitivity to GPU cost movement, and propose a guardrail (indexation floor/ceiling or credit mechanism).
2) Infra/Capacity: confirm we can reserve the ~120 vGPU units without blocking current Dedicated customers or causing risky oversubscription; propose fallback (burst pool / throttled burst) if market price spikes or usage varies.

Attached is the draft MAP and preliminary numbers from AE. I'm hopeful we can approve a controlled discount if we include a GPU-cost indexation clause and a limited burst / overcommit policy. If we can align today I want to send a revised commercial term to Brightlane tomorrow and schedule a procurement call with them Thurs.

Key constraints: customer wants SLA on baseline latency for embeddings and chat flows; we should not promise latency improvements that require aggressive overcommit.

Thanks —
Lauren
(lauren.bishop@redwood.com)
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Brightlane-MAP-v1.docx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity + pricing sensitivity for Brightlane (BL-4521)

Lauren —

Thanks for the summary. I ran a quick sensitivity model (attached) showing expected margin impact under three GPU market scenarios: base (0% change), +15% cost shock, and +30% sustained rise. High level: a straight 20% headline discount on list for 12 months is doable under base case but eats most margin under +15% unless we include one of the following: 

- Indexation clause (quarterly pricing true-up tied to a GPU cost index, capped at +10% pass-through to customer), or
- Floor/ceiling credit: if market GPU costs exceed X, customer gets rolling credits but not a price reduction, or
- Short-term surcharge: allow a temporary surcharge for up to 90 days in exceptional market shock, with a max of +12% and customer opt-in required.

My recommendation: approve a 15% committed-discount up front, plus an indexation trigger at +12% market move that allows us to request a temporary surcharge or offer a credit alternative. That keeps the deal competitive and protects margins.

I've attached BL-4521-financial-sensitivity.xlsx with the modeled scenarios and a proposed guardrail language snippet for legal.

Rishi
Head of Finance — Commercial
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity + pricing sensitivity for Brightlane (BL-4521)

Lauren / team —

Capacity notes from infra: 120 vGPU units (profiled on A100-equivalent) for 12 months is heavy but feasible if we earmark a combination of dedicated pools and a small burst buffer. Operationally I recommend:

- Reserve 100 units in a dedicated pool (pinned) to meet baseline SLA.
- Leave 20 units as a managed burst pool that can scale from our infra buffer for short spikes; bursts governed by a token bucket and optional throttle policy.
- Autoscaling policy on their route should prioritize baseline pool; if baseline is saturated, traffic can failover to a cheaper model variant (lower precision quantized model) rather than burst indefinitely.

Impact: this approach preserves our SLA for baseline calls, provides Brightlane with visibility into burst usage, and reduces risk of overcommit across Dedicated customers. We should also instrument per-route cost counters so we can reconcile actual GPU-hour consumption vs committed units monthly.

I'll drop a draft capacity-plan (pdf) in the thread. If finance wants a stricter floor, we can map expected utilization percentiles to committed units and tie some billing credits to underutilization.

Marcus Lin
VP, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity-plan-draft.pdf
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Reserved capacity + pricing sensitivity for Brightlane (BL-4521)

Team —

Legal input: we should accept indexation but keep it highly structured. Proposed redlines: 

1) Any market-cost pass-through must include a 60-day notice and a maximum annual increase of 12%.
2) Pass-through can only be applied if third-party GPU vendor published index shows >=12% sustained change over 30 days (not daily volatility).
3) Include a customer-friendly underutilization credit: if monthly committed consumption is <65% for >3 consecutive months, they receive a one-time credit applied to the next invoice (calculated at our incremental cost rate).
4) No unilateral surcharges without customer consent beyond emergency clause; emergency clause limited to declared force-majeure for supply chain shock.

I'll prepare a short redline and the DocuSign starter; linking the template: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/BL-4521-nda.

Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
